title: Turtle geometry
goal: I can find the turn angle and the inside angle of a regular polygon. I can predict what a turtle program draws.

learn.intro: A turtle moves forward and turns. Going once round a closed shape, it turns 360° in all and faces the way it began. In a regular polygon with n sides every turn is 360° ÷ n, and the inside angle is 180° − the turn.

example.problem: A turtle draws a regular polygon with 10 sides. Find the turn at each corner and the inside angle.
steps: Going once round, the turtle turns 360° in all.
There are 10 equal turns: 360° ÷ 10 = 36° at each corner.
The turn and the inside angle make a straight line: 180° − 36° = 144°.
example.answer: The turn is 36° and the inside angle is 144°.

howto.title: How to find the angles of a regular polygon
steps: Going once round, the turtle turns 360° in all.
All the inside angles of a polygon add to sides × 180 − 360.
Test it in code: repeat (sides) [move, turn].

try.text: A regular polygon has 9 sides. The turn at each corner is {b}° and the inside angle is {b}°.
try.explanation: 360° ÷ 9 = 40° for the turn. The inside angle is 180° − 40° = 140°.

items.text: Complete the table for regular polygons.
items.explanation: Turn = 360 ÷ sides and inside angle = 180 − turn. 5 sides: turn 72, inside 108. 12 sides: turn 30, inside 150. Turn 18: 360 ÷ 18 = 20 sides, inside 162. Inside 172: turn 8, and 360 ÷ 8 = 45 sides.

items.text: Program A: repeat 10 [move 40, turn ↻ 36].  Program B: repeat 12 [move 40, turn ↻ 30].  Program C: repeat 6 [move 40, turn ↻ 30]. One of them draws a regular polygon with inside angles of 150°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Program C turns {b}° in all, so its path   {circ:closes|does not close}

items.explanation: Inside 150° means a turn of 180° − 150° = 30°, and 360° ÷ 30° = 12 sides: Program B. Program C also turns 30°, but only 6 × 30 = 180° in all. That is half a turn, so the path does not close.

items.text: Trace the code. Write the total turned after each repeat, and the turn from the start direction (the total with every full 360° taken away).

parts.label: a
parts.text: After repeat 5 the turn from the start is {b}°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Is the turtle facing the way it started?   {circ:Yes|No}

items.explanation: The total turned grows by 100 each repeat: 100, 200, 300, 400, 500. Take away 360 when the total passes it: 500 − 360 = 140. The turtle faces 140° from its start direction, not 0°, so it is not facing the way it began.

items.text: A turtle walks round a closed shape with 5 sides. Its first 4 turns are 60°, 85°, 110° and 50°. It faces the way it started when it is back.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The 5 inside angles add up to {b}°.

items.explanation: All the turns add to 360°. The first 4 add to 305, so the last turn is 55° and the inside angle there is 125°. The 5 inside angles add to 5 × 180 − 360 = 540°.

items.text: A regular polygon has 18 sides. Find its angles.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The turn at each corner is {b}°.

parts.label: c
parts.text: All the inside angles add up to {b}°.

items.text: Circle each turn angle that draws a regular polygon. The number of sides must be a whole number.
items.explanation: The turn must divide 360 exactly. 360 ÷ 24 = 15 sides, ÷ 30 = 12, ÷ 45 = 8, ÷ 72 = 5 and ÷ 120 = 3 sides. 360 ÷ 50, 64, 100 and 150 are not whole numbers.

items.text: A turtle draws a star with 10 points and winds round the centre 3 times. It runs repeat 10 [move 80, turn ↻ ?].

parts.label: c
parts.text: The angle at each point is {b}°.

items.explanation: Going round 3 times, the turtle turns 3 × 360 = 1080° in all. 1080 ÷ 10 = 108° at each point. The angle at each point is 180 − 108 = 72°.

items.text: A turtle draws a regular shape with 30 sides. Fill in the blanks.
items.explanation: 30 sides need 30 repeats. The turn is 360 ÷ 30 = 12°. The inside angle is 180 − 12 = 168°.

items.text: This code draws a rectangle that is not a square. Predict it.
items.explanation: The rectangle has 4 right-angle turns: 4 × 90 = 360°. The turtle walks 100 + 50 + 100 + 50 = 300 steps. With 80 instead of 50: 100 + 80 + 100 + 80 = 360 steps.

items.text: Regular shapes fit around a point when their inside angles add to 360°. Check each group.
items.explanation: Triangle angle 60: 6 × 60 = 360. Square angle 90: 3 × 90 = 270, which is less than 360, so there is a gap of 90. Hexagon angle 120: 2 × 120 + 2 × 60 = 360.

items.text: Each inside angle is a few times the turn angle. Find the number of sides.
items.explanation: Turn + inside = 180. If the inside angle is k times the turn, then (k + 1) × turn = 180. k = 2: turn 60, so 6 sides. k = 5: turn 30, so 12 sides. k = 8: turn 20, so 18 sides.

items.text: A turtle repeats [move 40, turn ↻ 100] over and over. It stops when it first faces the start direction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: It first faces the start direction after {b} repeats.

parts.label: b
parts.text: By then it has turned {b}° in all.

items.hint: Try the total turned after 1, 2, 3 ... repeats.
items.explanation: After k repeats the total turned is 100k. It faces the start direction when 100k is a multiple of 360: 100k = 1800 first, at k = 18 (1800 ÷ 100). 1800 = 5 × 360, so it has turned round 5 times and draws an 18-point star.

items.text: All the inside angles of a regular polygon total 2340°.
items.hint: What do the inside angles of an n-sided shape add up to?
items.explanation: The sum of the inside angles is (n − 2) × 180, so n − 2 = 2340 ÷ 180 = 13 and n = 15. Each inside angle is 2340 ÷ 15 = 156°. The turn is 180 − 156 = 24°. Check: 360 ÷ 24 = 15.

items.text: A triangle, 2 squares and one more regular polygon fit around a point with no gap. All the sides are the same length.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The inside angle of the fourth shape is {b}°.

items.hint: The angles must add to 360. What is left for the fourth?
items.explanation: The angles are 60 + 90 + 90 = 240. 360 − 240 = 120° is left. A regular polygon with inside angle 120° has turn 60°, so 360 ÷ 60 = 6 sides: a hexagon.

items.text: The turtle starts at x = 0, y = 0, facing right. A turn ↻ is clockwise. Up means y increases.
items.hint: Make a table. Write x and y after each repeat.
items.explanation: Right 10, down 20, left 30, up 40 ends at x = 10 − 30 = −20, y = −20 + 40 = 20. The next 4 moves (50, 60, 70, 80) end at x = −40, y = 40. Each 4 repeats adds −20 to x and 20 to y, so 12 repeats end at (−60, 60).

items.text: The angle at each point of a star is 180° − the turn. Add up all the point angles.

parts.label: a
parts.text: 5-point star (turn 144°): the 5 point angles add to {b}°.

parts.label: b
parts.text: 8-point star, 3 times round: the 8 point angles add to {b}°.

parts.label: c
parts.text: 10-point star, 3 times round: each point angle is {b}° and they add to {b}°.

items.hint: Find each turn first. Then subtract it from 180 and multiply.
items.explanation: 5-point star: turn 144, point angle 36, and 5 × 36 = 180. 8-point star going round 3 times: turn 135, point angle 45, and 8 × 45 = 360. 10-point star going round 3 times: turn 108, point angle 72, and 10 × 72 = 720.

items.text: The turtle runs repeat 360 [move 1, turn ↻ 1].

parts.label: b
parts.text: The distance across the shape is about {b} steps (use 3.14, nearest whole number).

items.hint: The path round the shape is about 3.14 times the distance across.
items.explanation: 360 turns of 1° make one full turn, so the path closes. Inside angle 180 − 1 = 179°. The path is 360 steps long. Round ≈ 3.14 × across, so across ≈ 360 ÷ 3.14 = 114.6, about 115.
items.beyond: A polygon that looks like a circle

items.text: A regular polygon has 40 sides. Each turn is {b}° and each inside angle is {b}°.
items.explanation: 360 ÷ 40 = 9°. The inside angle is 180 − 9 = 171°.

items.text: A turtle turns 10° at each corner of a regular polygon. The polygon has {b} sides.
A regular polygon has inside angles of 156° each. It has {b} sides.
items.explanation: The turn is 180 − 156 = 24°, and 360 ÷ 24 = 15 sides.

items.text: A turtle goes round a closed 4-sided shape. Its first 3 turns are 95°, 80° and 105°. The last turn is {b}°.
items.explanation: The turns add to 360. 95 + 80 + 105 = 280, so the last turn is 360 − 280 = 80°.
